statement: You are given an array nums of non-negative integers and start at index 0. From index i you may jump forward to any index from i + 1 up to i + nums[i].
Return the minimum number of jumps needed to reach the last index, n − 1. If the last index cannot be reached at all, return −1.

Think of it as a breadth-first search done in place: the indices reachable with j jumps form a contiguous range, and the next range ends at the farthest point any index in the current range can jump to. Count the ranges until one contains n − 1, which takes O(n) time.

examples.explanation: Jump from index 0 to index 1, then from index 1 (value 3) straight to the last index. One jump is not enough, because index 0 reaches only as far as index 2.
Every path lands on index 3, whose value is 0, and nothing gets past it, so the last index is unreachable.
